_about: Open and crowd data sources for DAStastic: what each needs, costs and allows. Checked on the providers' own pages 2026-10-28; the map, terrain, address-search, building-outline and radar services 2026-11-02 (header-only or anonymous requests; no sign-ups). 'updater' names the Data & updates sources it covers; 'keys' the settings it needs; 'status' says whether DAStastic uses it.

sources.name: FCC ULS licences, ASR towers, broadcast
sources.what: Licensed transmitters, towers and broadcast stations
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: FCC market licences (carrier spectrum)
sources.what: Who holds which block in each market: l_market and l_cell, with the rules' band plans (47 CFR 22.905, 24.229, 27.5)
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: NOAA Weather Radio
sources.what: NWR transmitters and the counties each warns
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: FAA aviation frequencies (NASR)
sources.what: Towers, ATIS, approach, navaids
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: Signal Identification Wiki
sources.what: What a signal could be
sources.terms: Read on this PC; the catalog is never exported
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: Artemis signal database (Ares Valley)
sources.what: Open-source signal identification app and its offline database of 500+ signals, built from the Signal Identification Wiki, with each signal's waterfall picture and audio clip
sources.cost: Free (release v74 is a 302 MB download, about 290 MB unpacked)
sources.terms: App GPL-3.0; the database is Signal Identification Wiki content: read on this PC, never exported
sources.area: Catalog (by frequency, bandwidth and mode, not by place)
sources.status: In DAStastic: each Signal ID Wiki match shows its waterfall and plays its audio (map details, field log). Data & updates, Artemis signal database, downloads it (off until you switch it on)

sources.name: WiGLE
sources.where_key: wigle.net > Account > API token (shows the API name and token)
sources.what: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and cell sightings
sources.key: Free key with a WiGLE account
sources.cost: Free (non-commercial only; commercial licensing is suspended)
sources.terms: Personal, research or educational use only; no redistribution
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: OpenCelliD
sources.where_key: my.opencellid.org > your account: the access token
sources.what: Cell towers: cell IDs, positions, ranges; country downloads
sources.cost: Free (1,000 requests a day); commercial plans unpriced
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0: credit OpenCelliD with a link
sources.area: Yes (box up to 4 sq km, 50 cells a request); whole-country downloads
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: RepeaterBook
sources.where_key: Granted by RepeaterBook after you request a token
sources.what: Amateur and GMRS repeaters
sources.key: Free token, on request and approval
sources.cost: Free for approved non-commercial use; commercial needs paid terms
sources.terms: Personal use; its policy discourages tools that mix it with other sources, and repeater maps need written permission
sources.status: In DAStastic (check the token's approved use)

sources.name: RadioReference web service
sources.what: Trunked systems, sites, talk groups
sources.key: App key (free on approval) plus a Premium subscription for every user
sources.cost: Premium $30/year ($15 for 6 months, $60 for 2 years); dashboards need a paid licence (price not stated)
sources.terms: The free key is for radio-programming tools only
sources.area: By county; callsign radius under 3 mi
sources.status: Not added: needs Premium and a paid licence. DAStastic links to it instead.

sources.name: OpenSky Network (ADS-B)
sources.what: Live aircraft positions
sources.terms: Any automated or live use needs a written licence
sources.status: Not added: needs OpenSky's written licence first

sources.name: aisstream.io (AIS)
sources.what: Live ship positions
sources.terms: No terms published; no direct browser connections
sources.status: In DAStastic: the map's Ships (AIS, live) layer, for the owner only (Cody's PC, and his admin login on the 24/7 server); streams only while the layer is on

sources.name: aprs.fi
sources.what: APRS stations
sources.terms: Apps using it must be free and public; credit and link
sources.status: Not added: no area search, and a private tool doesn't meet its terms

sources.name: beaconDB
sources.what: Wi-Fi / cell geolocation
sources.terms: Public domain (dumps planned)
sources.area: No (turns what you see into a position)
sources.status: Not added: can't list emitters in an area yet

sources.name: FCC Broadband Data Collection: mobile coverage
sources.what: Each carrier's modelled 3G / 4G / 5G coverage and signal level, as 0.1 km2 hexagons
sources.key: Free FCC account for the API; downloads open
sources.terms: US government data
sources.area: Per state (the carrier-coverage states in Data & updates)
sources.status: In DAStastic
sources.where_key: broadbandmap.fcc.gov > sign in > Manage API Access > Generate (the token pairs with your FCC sign-in email)

sources.name: FCC Broadband Data Collection: coverage checks, fixed wireless, link budgets
sources.what: The FCC's resolved mobile coverage challenges, verifications and audits (where claimed coverage was tested on the ground), who offers licensed, unlicensed and LBR fixed wireless where, and each carrier's filed link budgets (frequencies, bandwidths, antennas) and propagation tools
sources.key: Free FCC account for the API (the same token as carrier coverage)
sources.terms: US government data; the API allows 10 calls a minute
sources.area: H3 cells of about 0.7 km2 (checks, fixed wireless); per provider (link budgets)
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-03: Cell sites, under Carrier coverage at the pin, and How modelled per carrier. Left out: wired broadband, summaries, raw coverage polygons (about 82 GB), the Funding Map, and Location Fabric points (CostQuest licence)
sources.where_key: broadbandmap.fcc.gov > sign in > Manage API Access > Generate

sources.name: Map tiles and terrain kept for mission areas
sources.what: The four USGS base maps (to zoom 16; shaded relief to zoom 13) and AWS terrain tiles for each mission area, kept so maps and coverage estimates work there with no signal
sources.cost: Free (about 1.3 GB of disk an area)
sources.terms: USGS: public domain, tile export allowed (checked 2026-11-03); terrain: AWS open data, credit Tilezen's sources. OpenStreetMap and Esri tiles are never kept
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-03

sources.name: FCC Equipment Authorization (FCC ID)
sources.what: A device's grants (look up any FCC ID), and every grantee code's company, kept on this PC
sources.terms: US government data
sources.status: In DAStastic: grantee codes download with the data sources; Look up an FCC ID in Data & updates; makers in Search

sources.name: SatNOGS
sources.what: Satellite transmitters and ground stations
sources.terms: CC BY-SA 4.0
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: RadioID.net
sources.what: DMR / NXDN radio IDs
sources.terms: No mirroring, bulk export or competing directory
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-03: look-ups only, from a DMR or NXDN reading's details (one ID when asked, kept 30 days)

sources.name: PSKReporter
sources.what: Live HF reception reports
sources.terms: Not stated; poll at most every 5 minutes
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: Reverse Beacon Network
sources.what: CW / digital skimmer spots
sources.terms: Free for study and analysis
sources.status: Could add (daily files)

sources.name: wspr.live (WSPRnet)
sources.what: WSPR propagation spots
sources.terms: Non-commercial; results free for everyone; 20 requests a minute
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: The Things Network gateways (Packet Broker)
sources.what: LoRaWAN gateway locations
sources.terms: Not stated
sources.status: In DAStastic

sources.name: Helium hotspots
sources.what: IoT hotspot locations (blurred)
sources.terms: Not stated
sources.area: No (paged list of about a million)
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-03: active Helium IoT hotspots for each mission area; reads the whole network (about 190 MB) a week, so on for the 24/7 server and off by default

sources.name: Meshtastic map (meshmap.net)
sources.what: Meshtastic nodes that share their position
sources.terms: Data terms not stated
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-03: the Meshtastic mesh radios layer, for each mission area (one 4 MB list a day)

sources.name: Ookla open data
sources.what: Mobile speed-test performance tiles
sources.terms: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: non-commercial, credit Ookla
sources.status: Could add (bulk, non-commercial)

sources.name: KiwiSDR / WebSDR lists
sources.what: Remote receivers near a site
sources.terms: Not stated
sources.status: Not added: no documented list to read

sources.name: CellMapper
sources.what: Crowd cell maps
sources.terms: Personal viewing only; no mirroring
sources.status: Not added: its terms allow viewing only. DAStastic links to it.

sources.name: FCC 911 PSAP registry
sources.what: 911 call centres
sources.terms: US government data
sources.status: In DAStastic: the FCC's registry as of 2026-10-30 (8,933 PSAPs, orphaned and secondary ones marked), downloaded by a person from https://www.fcc.gov/general/9-1-1-master-psap-registry (fcc.gov refuses automated clients) and read by tools/psap_registry.py; the opendata copy (rows to 2017-10-10) only without it. Placed at town or county centres (no addresses in the registry)

sources.name: FCC Protected FSS Earth Station Registration
sources.what: C-band satellite earth stations (3.6 to 4.2 GHz receive sites): position, pointing, gain, height
sources.terms: US government data
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-02: about 470 sites, updated daily by the FCC

sources.name: FCC signal booster registrations (Class B)
sources.what: Every Class B signal booster registered with the FCC (47 CFR 90.219(d)(5)): where it is, the building's address and description, its call signs and frequencies, the company and the dates. The registrants' named contacts are kept apart (booster_contact), on the server and Cody's PC only, for the admin
sources.terms: US government data (FCC); the item carries no licence text
sources.area: Bulk: the FCC's public ArcGIS layer, pages of 2,000 (about 10 requests), checked weekly and downloaded only when the layer changed
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-08, on by default: a DAS job's Existing system (registered at the building, and within the pre-survey's radius), the pre-survey (boosters on the systems' channels), DAS Prospects (existing system) and the map's layer Signal boosters (FCC registered)

sources.name: FCC ULS microwave applications (a_micro.zip)
sources.what: Microwave links filed but not yet granted (application status 2, pending)
sources.terms: US government data
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-02, off by default (about 445 MB): about 2,300 pending links, drawn dashed on the Microwave backhaul layer

sources.name: FCC ULS daily change files
sources.what: Each day's new, changed, cancelled and expired land mobile (private l_lp, commercial l_lc, broadcast auxiliary l_lb), paging (l_pg), coast and aviation ground (l_cg) and 800 MHz cellular (l_cl) licences and antenna structure registrations (r_tow, towers), each where its weekly file is loaded, and the land mobile applications filed (a_lp), every day of the week
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.area: Bulk daily files (data.fcc.gov/download/pub/uls/daily/), about 20 to 400 KB each, each replaced a week later
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-08, on by default: changed licences go into the licence data the next day (Sunday's full file still wins); applications filed, not granted, show apart on Agencies and the DAS pre-survey

sources.name: OpenStreetMap map tiles
sources.what: The Street base map
sources.terms: Tile policy: light use, credit OpenStreetMap, honour caching; no bulk downloads, prefetching or offline use
sources.status: In DAStastic: the Street base map

sources.name: USGS The National Map
sources.what: Satellite, satellite + labels, topo and terrain relief base maps
sources.terms: US government public domain; USGS asks for credit
sources.status: In DAStastic: the four USGS base maps

sources.name: Esri World Imagery
sources.what: Hi-res satellite base map (the ATAK map style starts on it)
sources.terms: Esri Master License Agreement; credit Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics; not for exporting tiles to use offline
sources.status: In DAStastic: the Satellite hi-res (Esri) base map

sources.name: US Census Bureau TIGERweb
sources.what: County and state lines
sources.terms: US government public data
sources.area: Map tiles; one point query per DAS job
sources.status: In DAStastic: the County + state lines layer; a DAS job's county and city (the AHJ guess)

sources.name: Terrain Tiles on AWS (Tilezen)
sources.what: Ground elevation: USGS 3DEP in the US, SRTM and others elsewhere
sources.terms: AWS open data; credit the sources in Tilezen's attribution list
sources.status: In DAStastic: terrain profiles and coverage estimates; tiles already fetched are kept for use with no signal

sources.name: Photon address search (komoot)
sources.what: Addresses and places for the Pin box
sources.terms: Public demo server: "please be fair"; heavy use is throttled; no availability promise. OpenStreetMap data
sources.status: In DAStastic: addresses in the Pin box's search

sources.name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap)
sources.what: Building outlines; road and rail tunnels
sources.terms: Main server: under 10,000 queries and 1 GB a day; OpenStreetMap data (ODbL), credit OpenStreetMap; tunnel prospects kept off the public packs
sources.status: In DAStastic: DAS jobs' building outlines, tunnels near a job and tunnel prospects (public servers asked at once)

sources.name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet: NEXRAD
sources.what: Live weather radar, refreshed every 5 minutes
sources.terms: No terms published for the tile service
sources.status: In DAStastic: the map's Weather radar (NEXRAD, live) layer

sources.name: USFA National Fire Department Registry
sources.what: 27,117 fire departments (HQ and mail address, phone, website, county, type, stations) and 8,092 station addresses; no coordinates (placed by ZIP centre)
sources.terms: US government work: the registry says the general public can use the data; FEMA: free of copyright, may be copied and distributed (read 2026-11-04). Frozen: no updates after June 2026 (NERIS is the current list)
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-04: a DAS job's AHJ guess (the fire departments covering the address)

sources.name: FCC ECFS filings (rules watch)
sources.what: New filings (comments, ex partes, orders, notices) in the dockets that change DAS and ERCES work: signal boosters (WT 10-4), 4.9 GHz (WP 07-100), T-band (PS 13-42), the Covered List (WC 18-89), equipment authorization integrity (ET 24-136), NG911 (PS 21-479), 911 location (PS 07-114)
sources.terms: FCC API Terms of Service (accepted by Cody for DAStastic 11/8); attribution shown with the filings
sources.area: Daily, the newest 25 filings per docket
sources.status: In DAStastic from 2026-11-08, on by default: waits for the api.data.gov key
